runner: omp (Oh My Pi) v18.1.13, --no-tools --no-lsp, one session per seat

findings.where: Package section 4 (rule inventory) vs. section 3 — 22 of 35 contracts
findings.what: Twenty-two contracts declare a "Refusal classes" section but the inventory records "No closed refusal set is declared in this document" (artifact-write-receipt, autobuild-run, bounded-loop, clearance-manifest, debate, doctor-report, evidence-manifest, external-source-snapshot, governance-bundle, housekeeping, human-decision, provider-preflight, reflect-cost-watch, requirement-revision, sdk-write-api, stage-carriers, static-analysis, verify-doc, walkthrough, work-type-gates, plus epic-planning-ref/project-instructions-lock/tickets-manifest which have none at all), so for the majority of the contract surface the refusal vocabulary is open-ended and nothing in this package shows a validator that can enumerate or check it — a guarantee ("fail-closed with a named refusal") whose mechanism is absent from the reviewable material.

Several park reasons used as workflow states in the resume table (`planning_ref_init_invalid`, `planning_ref_capability_missing`, `planning_ref_foreign_movement`, `planning_candidate_keepalive_invalid`, `planning_candidate_base_stale`, `planning_publication_invalid`, `planning_publication_corrupt`, `planning_signing_unavailable`, `artifact_mapping_required`, `alignment_policy_out_of_scope`, `alignment_record_stale`, `tickets_manifest_invalid/stale`, `protocol_lock_invalid`, `arena_fallback_required`, `implementation_scope_invalid`, `brief_alignment_required`, `core_flow_decision_required`, `tech_plan_readiness_required`, `tickets_breakdown_alignment_required`) belong to no closed refusal set in section 4 — `epic-planning-ref.md` and `project-instructions-lock.md` explicitly declare none — so the set of reachable park states is asserted by prose only and no listed schema in section 3 is named as its validator.

The two cross-family rules contradict each other in the mixed-authorship case: §3 requires the Lead to be "другой семьи относительно всех авторов и всех агентов, реально исправлявших артефакт" and falls through to a human when no such family exists, while §6's reviewer-order table for `Codex` omits GPT entirely ("Kimi, затем Grok") and for `Claude` lists GPT/Kimi/Grok — the filters are stated over different sets (author-only vs. author∪fixer) in the same document, so a Codex-authored artifact fixed by Kimi yields different legal reviewers under the two tables.

findings.where: Section 5 (Evidence) — "Every runtime module in `src/host/` was mutation-tested"
findings.what: The mutation-testing claim outruns the package: no mutant counts, no killed/survived totals and no per-module figures are given here — they are deferred to "the pull request that introduced each module", which is not in the package and not digest-pinned, so the strongest correctness claim in the evidence section is unverifiable from the frozen artifact under review.

`complete=true` is asserted against an undisclosed denominator: neither the fault matrix's total group count nor its enumeration appears in the package (only the digest of `resources/clean-room-e2e/fault-matrix.schema.json`), so "16 covered, complete" cannot be distinguished from "16 of 16 defined by the same run that reports it" — self-certifying completeness.

findings.where: 02-architecture.md §2 ("Current autosk не даёт three required surfaces: ADR-014, ADR-023, ADR-025") vs. §5/§7
findings.what: The whole design is load-bearing on three upstream primitives (creation identity, signed authority/intent, workflow custody) that the document itself states the pinned autosk `5163f00` does not implement; the package pins that same upstream commit in section 5 and reports `deps:daemon=ok`, so the clean-room run cannot have exercised `UserDecisionRecord` signing, protected authority/dependency/intent heads, or `orchestrateChildBatch` — the primary guarantee ("model cannot self-approve; approval requires a daemon-attributed signed record") has no mechanism at the reviewed commit, only a preflight that blocks.

The mandatory "separate OS boundary or hardware enclave inaccessible to model accessibility/ptrace/keychain" is declared a preflight assertion, but nothing in this package — no contract in section 4, no schema in section 3, no clean-room step in section 5 — evaluates it; `harness:identity=ok` is not stated to include a signer-isolation probe, so a refusal class for "no enforceable boundary" exists in prose ("blocks model launch") with no named producer.

findings.where: Package section 2 question 3 vs. section 5 ("What is not claimed")
findings.what: Issue #10 criterion 2 (declarative workflow graph) is "deferred to this design gate" — i.e. the panel is asked to accept a design gate for a criterion whose satisfaction is the gate itself — while the package supplies no artifact named as that workflow graph among the 96 files, making the deferral unclosable by this panel.

findings.where: 02-architecture.md §5 ("Автономный governance bundle") — 13-file digest vs. the listed tree
findings.what: The bundle tree lists `agent-selection-guide.md`, `bundle-manifest.json`, `bundle-attestation.json` and 12 protocol files under `protocol/`, and the digest is defined over "these 13 файлов" (guide + 12 protocol) while `protocol.lock.json` is said to record "SHA-256 каждого из 13 нормативных файлов"; the arithmetic only closes if the manifest and attestation are excluded, which the text asserts for the content preimage but never states for the lock's 13 — an off-by-one in the identity definition of the governance root of trust.

The pre-freeze `pending_validation_proof` (`candidate_tree_oid=null`, explicitly "не является authority") and the post-freeze `final_validation_receipt` are described in two places with different actors and orderings (core-flows: freeze step re-reads the exact tree; architecture: `freeze_artifact` calls `validateTicketsCandidateGitTree`), and neither text says what happens when the two validations disagree — the failure edge for the one place mutable-path and Git-tree reads can diverge is unspecified.

Integration step 6 cleans up with `force=false` and preserves a dirty workspace "для решения человеком", but the epic is then said to transition to `done` in step 7; the resume table's `Dirty cleanup -> cleanup` row implies the epic must instead park, so the terminal state after a dirty cleanup is contradictory between the happy path and the recovery table.

findings.where: 02-architecture.md §3 ("штатный worker pool по умолчанию имеет четыре места") vs. §3 fairness paragraph
findings.what: The panel's parallelism guarantee rests on a default pool of four while the same section admits the pool is global and configurable and that one project's panel "может временно занять все worker slots"; with multiple active Epics the four-seat fan-in can deadlock against itself (parent blocked by four children that cannot be scheduled) and the document defers any admission/fairness layer until "доказанный starvation" — a liveness hazard with no mechanism, only an observation.

findings.where: Package section 3 — coverage of the review
findings.what: Only 2 of 96 files are reproduced in full; the other 94 (including every schema that would show whether the prose rules are actually machine-checkable, and all 35 contracts) are present as truncated 16-hex-digit digest prefixes that cannot be recomputed or checked against the candidate digest, so no seat can verify the section-4 rule inventory against the documents it summarizes.

The editorial Code Review exemption is defined by a "deterministic editorial classification" whose rule set is never enumerated here (only its exclusions), so the boundary between an exempt editorial change and a `behavior-defining документ` rests on an unnamed classifier version.

The round cap is stated once as a hard human handoff and once as a user-waivable exception with a "daemon cap decision", but neither text says whether the new cap is bounded, so an unbounded review loop is reachable by repeated cap decisions.

seats.read: The full panel package: section 1 (version/digest table), section 2 (the four questions), section 3 (the 96-path/digest inventory, read as a list — digests are truncated prefixes and were not recomputed), section 4 (all 35 contracts' section headings and their declared-or-absent closed refusal sets, cross-checked against the park reasons and refusal names appearing in the full-text documents), section 5 (tests, mutation-testing claim, clean-room e2e table and step list, fault-matrix line, and the three 'not claimed' items), and section 6 in full — both 01-core-flows.md (all 9 sections including the alignment table, the resume table, and the exceptions table) and 02-architecture.md (all 10 sections including Git/ref-custody, planning publication adapter, tickets manifest, storage layout, identity preimages, worktree/read-only review, and the not-built list). Cross-checks performed: refusal names in the full texts against the section-4 closed sets; the two cross-family routing tables against each other; the governance-bundle file count against its digest definition; the pinned upstream commit in section 5 against the ADR-014/023/025 gap stated in 02-architecture.md §2/§3.
seats.not_read: The 94 files that are digest-only: all 35 contract documents' actual text (only their section titles and refusal sets as summarized in section 4), 03-technical-plan.md, 04-decisions.md, README.md, and all 57 JSON schemas under resources/. I could not verify any digest (the package gives 16-hex-digit prefixes only, and I have no tools), could not open the repository at eef3b07 or the clean-room report 22d5a0d4…, could not see the fault matrix's total group count, and could not see the mutation-testing counts, which the package places in per-module pull requests outside this material. Findings about those files are therefore about what the package itself states or omits, not about their contents.

findings.what: Нормативная последовательность выполняет CAS пользовательской target branch до aggregate verification всего Epic, не требуя предварительного aggregate PASS на exact final tree; [INFERENCE] несовместимые по совокупному поведению Tickets могут попасть в целевую ветку до обнаружения ошибки, поэтому aggregate gate должен предшествовать target CAS и связываться с проверенной staging identity.

findings.where: 01-core-flows.md §2 «Согласование решений человеком» и §8, строка «Brief framing не согласован»
findings.what: §2 прямо запрещает policy утверждать product framing Brief, однако recovery-таблица §8 разрешает продолжение по «daemon UserDecisionRecord framing либо current exact policy той же identity», задавая противоречивое условие одного approval gate.

Сводка clean-room фиксирует upstream commit, reproduced source tree и report digest, но не показывает identity фактически загруженного autosk-flow и её связь с проверяемым main tree/candidate digest, поэтому приведённого overall=ok недостаточно для подтверждения end-to-end именно замороженной версии расширения.

findings.what: After accept, Core Flows specifies only local merge-OID plus daemon integrateApproved target CAS; Architecture says local CAS is not the default and delivery-profile (PR, merge queue, signed commits, DCO) is bound before first implementation dispatch, but §7 never consults that profile and gives those modes no completion path.

IntegrationAuthorizationRecord is the only token that may skip human accept and CAS-advance the user's target ref, yet the candidate has no contract path and no schema for it (unlike creation-grant and the planning-publication ops).

The load-bearing rule that unreferenced prose is not material authority depends on one fenced JSON block plus a deterministic projector, and neither a material-decision nor a projector schema appears in the candidate.

Architecture says current autosk lacks ADR-014/023/025 and must preflight-block every model workflow until they exist; §5 reports clean-room overall=ok with harness:creation and harness:identity on pinned 5163f00 and neither reconciles that dependency nor records the mandatory signer OS-boundary proof.

The inventory treats Arena-or-Debate as one choice with a 3–5 position roster; Core Flows Arena is two family-isolated implementation candidates plus optional C, and the §8 resume table has Arena parks but no Debate lifecycle.
Both are marked v1 load-bearing in 01/02 and §8 names many planning_* / tickets_manifest_* parks, but this package records no closed refusal set for either document.

The same digest specifies a closed four-way path-role classifier until issue #14 and also a full Artifact Registry contract with a different classifier and closed refusals, with no migration rule in the reproduced text.
1729 passing tests and per-module mutation testing of src/host/ are asserted here; this package has no transcript, and mutation counts are explicitly left in pull requests outside the package.
